about: Reviewed 'Did you know?' lines for feed cards. match: taxon (iNaturalist species or genus name), title (a word in the card title; non-iNaturalist cards unless source is set) or topic. Only status 'approved' goes live. Edit with: node scripts/review.mjs

items.text: Its gel-coated stems glow a steady yellow-green in the dark (the caps don't), which is why it's called the eternal light mushroom.
Called goblin gold: round cells in this moss act like tiny lenses, gathering the faintest light in dark places and reflecting a greenish-gold glow.
Nicknamed bug-on-a-stick and elf-cap moss: what you notice is its big, lopsided spore capsule perched on a stalk.
Most mosses trust the wind with their spores. This one makes brightly coloured, scented capsules that bring insects in to carry them away.
It drifts across the open ocean upside down, held up by the water's surface tension and a gas bubble in its stomach.
The sea bunny's 'ears' are rhinophores, the sensory organs a nudibranch uses to sense the water around it.
The smallest bird alive: a male is about 5.5 cm long and weighs around 2 grams.
In his courtship dive, a male reaches about 27 metres per second: 385 of his own body lengths every second.
It flies about 3,200 km on its migrations: an enormous journey for a bird you could hold in one hand.
Some fly nonstop across the Gulf of Mexico on migration, a journey of around 800 km over open water.
The monarchs flying south in autumn are not the ones that flew north in spring: it takes two to three generations to make the trip back north.
The largest butterfly in the world: females can have wings 25 to 28 cm across.
Clearwing moths feed at flowers by day and are often mistaken for hummingbirds.
This tardigrade went to space: in an ESA experiment it was exposed to the radiation, near-vacuum and deep cold of orbit, and some survived.
Not one animal but a colony: it is made of many smaller, genetically identical units called zooids, each with its own job, working as one.
A close relative, Turritopsis dohrnii, can turn back into its young polyp stage after growing up, which is why it's called the immortal jellyfish.
A relative, Ramazzottius varieornatus, makes a protein called Dsup that shields its DNA. Human cells given it in the lab tolerated about 40% more X-ray radiation.
When their world dries out, tardigrades curl into a 'tun' and suspend their metabolism, then come back to life when water returns.
Water bears are ancient: the earliest known tardigrade fossil is from the Cambrian, around 500 million years ago.
Slime molds have no brain, yet one species, Physarum polycephalum, can find the shortest path through a maze.
'Nudibranch' means 'naked gills': many breathe through feathery plumes worn openly on their backs.
The hum is their wings: hovering hummingbirds beat them from about 12 times a second in the largest species to 99 in the smallest.
These single cells build elaborate skeletons, usually of silica, the stuff of glass. Ernst Haeckel's 1887 drawings of them are still famous.
Each of an adult dragonfly's eyes has nearly 24,000 facets (ommatidia).
A mushroom is just the fruit. The fungus itself is a mycelium, a branching web of threads in soil or wood that can carry water and electrical signals.
Small but mighty: mosses absorb an estimated 6.4 billion tons of carbon every year, and they have no flowers or seeds at all.
Jellyfish have drifted through the oceans for at least 500 million years, making them the oldest animal group with multiple organs.
Particles from the Sun excite oxygen and nitrogen high in the atmosphere, which then give off green, red and purple light.
Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a giant storm that people have watched since at least 1831. A century ago it was about three times as wide as Earth.
Mars has Olympus Mons, a volcano about 21 km high: roughly two and a half times the height of Everest.
Yellowstone National Park alone is home to half of all the geysers on Earth.
Glacier ice glows blue because thick, bubble-free ice absorbs some of the red light passing through it.
There may be between 200 billion and 2 trillion galaxies in the observable universe.
